verdict.reasoning: Patient reports fever and sweats for about a week: 'I've been struggling with fever for the past week... I'm really hot and sweaty all the time.'

Hot/cold: 'you're having periods of when you're feeling hot, and also periods when you're feeling cold as well.' Myalgias: 'I'm aching all over really, my muscles are really aching.' Nausea and decreased appetite: 'I'm feeling quite nauseous... so I've not been able to eat very much.'
Limited fluids: 'I have been drinking but it's been quite a small amount.' Fatigue: 'yeah, just generally quite tired and unwell.'

OTC meds and partial relief: 'I've been trying to, like, take ibuprofen and paracetamol... but it's not really helping... Perhaps slightly, yes, but I'm still experiencing these symptoms, so, it does take the edge off a bit.'

Denials: cough/cold/sore throat – 'Mmm, not those sort of symptoms, really.' Ear pain – 'no, my ears are fine.' Diarrhoea – 'not really no.' Neck stiffness – 'no. My neck's been fine.' Rash – 'I haven't noticed any rashes, no.' Urinary symptoms (dysuria/frequency) – 'no, there's been no problems there' and 'I don't think so, no it's been fairly regular.' Coryza is reasonably inferred from ‘not those sort of symptoms’ along with no cough/cold/sore throat.
Baseline headaches: 'It's something that I've struggled with through, years really, just related to a screen use, or... changes in weather patterns.'

Chronic back pain and physio: 'I often have problems with back pain' and 'I'm under a physiotherapist at the moment for that.' Cause: 'they've said that it's... related to long periods of time sitting at a desk, and just, bad posture.'

Travel: 'I went to Vietnam. Uh, I came back four weeks ago now.' Rural trekking/cycling: 'We toured to several different parts of the country, and uh, the countryside... We were sort of trekking and, um, cycling, uh, through the farmland.'

Malaria prophylaxis details: 'I did, yes.' Daily: 'I think it was daily.' Additional tablet: 'I think it was, uh another one that I took on top of the first one.' Name unknown: 'Ooo, I can't remember now, off the top of my head.'
Chronic back pain: 'I often have problems with back pain' and 'I've been struggling with back pain for quite a while.'
Current medication: 'Uh, just Seroxat.' (Seroxat is paroxetine.)
Pollen allergy/hay fever: 'No, I've just really pollen allergy. That's all I have.' Doctor clarifies: 'OK, so hay fever.' Patient: 'Yes, yeah, just hay fever.'
Father MI and age: 'the main one would be, um, heart attack. My, my father passed away of that.' and 'Um, sixty eight, I think. Yeah.' Myocardial infarction is synonymous with heart attack.
Occupation and vaccinations: 'I work as a nurse.' and 'you're up to date with all the vaccinations, Hepatitis B, and that kind of thing?'; Patient: 'Yes, indeed. Yeah.'
Smoking, alcohol, exercise: 'No, I'm not.' (smoker) 'Mmm, moderate alcohol intake. Yeah, I don't drink too much.' and 'I try and do, uh, some moderate physical exercise a few times a week.'
Work impacted by fatigue: 'I'm really struggling quite a lot at work at the moment. It's been quite difficult, feeling so, uh, tired all the time.'

Summary matches: fever with sweats for 7 days – 'fever for the past week... really hot and sweaty'; post-travel Vietnam – 'I went to Vietnam... came back four weeks ago'; malaria/exotic infection vs other – Doctor: 'we need to think about things like malaria or other exotic infections as well.' Viral illness is a reasonable differential given non-focal febrile illness.

No localizing features: respiratory – 'no cough or cold or sore throat'; urinary – 'no problems there... not at all' and frequency denied; GI – 'have you had any diarrhoea?' 'not really no'; meningitic – 'Have you got any neck stiffness at all?' 'no.' This supports absence of localizing respiratory, urinary, GI, or meningitic signs.

Urgent in-person exam and labs guided by findings: 'we're gonna need to bring you into one of our clinics. Examine , and we're gonna need to arrange some blood tests as well.' and 'the urgency of those blood tests depends partly on what we find when we examine you.'
Tests ordered: 'I'll be asking for something called thick and thin blood films, to check for malaria. And inflammatory markers and things like those.'

Admin details and number to call: 'I will send a message to one of our admin team members asking them to book you in. And if you can ring the number that I leave in your consultation notes, after a few minutes, and then they'll slot you in.'
Alternative A&E: 'you could actually just attend a local A and E' if central clinic is inconvenient.
Off work advice: 'I don't think you can go into work, uh, until we've sorted this out. And we, we, we need to sort this out sooner rather than later.'
